title: Add JSONSchema structured response_format with strict mode and OpenAI-compatibility
author: Sofia Ramirez
description: Motivation: Add first-class support for JSONSchema-driven structured output (response_format=json_schema) with an opt-in strict mode that enforces validation at runtime and returns machine-readable error payloads. This builds on previous structured-output work and aligns Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer with community expectations for schema enforcement. Design notes: - Introduce response_format.type = "json_schema" and response_format.options.strict = true|false. - Validation happens post-generation against the provided schema; if strict mode is enabled and validation fails, the runtime will return a standardized error object (error.type="schema_validation_failed") including path-level error details and suggested remediation where available. - OpenAI compatibility: the API surface also accepts OpenAI-style function/schema payloads and maps them to the same validation flow, preserving fields like name/description and returning errors in a shape compatible with existing clients. - Backwards compatible: default behavior is permissive (strict=false). When strict=true we return 422 with structured error; when strict=false we attach validation warnings to response metadata and allow the output through. Changes included: server/api/response_format.go (new handler logic), server/validation/jsonschema.go (validation engine with AJV-inspired rules), openai_compat/mapper.go (mapping OpenAI function/schema inputs), sdk-python/redwood/response.py (public SDK helpers to declare response_format), sdk-typescript/src/response.ts (type definitions and helper), console/docs/structured-output.md (docs + examples), tests/* (unit and integration tests). Migration: - Customers using response_format=json_schema should opt-in to strict mode after validating their prompt/test suites. - For OpenAI-compat clients, schema fields are accepted transparently. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4523) - [x] Implementation for server + compatibility layer - [x] Unit tests for validation paths and error formatting - [x] Integration tests with streaming + non-streaming codepaths - [x] Docs and SDK helpers - [x] QA signoff (Priya)

review_comments: Liam Chen (reviewer): Can we avoid blocking streaming responses when strict mode is enabled? Streaming is an important SLO for low-latency apps. Author (Sofia Ramirez): We implemented streaming compatibility by running incremental validation against completed top-level fields and only gating the final commit when strict=true; added tests to cover partial stream + final validation. Priya Nair (reviewer): Error payload looks good but can we include a stable error.code field for programmatic handling? Author: Added error.code="schema_validation_failed" and included single-line suggested_remediation entries where available. Evan Brooks (reviewer): Please ensure OpenAI-compat mapping preserves argument names and types. Author: Mapper retains name/description and maps types with conservative casting; documented edge-cases in console/docs. Priya: Approved after followups. Liam: Approved. Evan: Approved.
tests: Unit: validation rules, error shaping, permissive vs strict. Integration: end-to-end response_format=json_schema with streaming and non-streaming; OpenAI-compat function call mapping. Added ~35 new unit tests and 4 integration tests that run in CI matrix for node/python SDKs.
ci_checks: linux-unit-tests: pass, linux-integration-tests: pass, lint: pass (python/ts/go), e2e: pass (staging), security-scan: pass
release_notes: Added response_format="json_schema" with optional strict mode to validate generated outputs against a provided JSON Schema. Strict mode returns structured 422 error payloads on validation failures. OpenAI-compat layer now accepts function/schema payloads and maps them to response_format=json_schema. Backward-compatible by default (strict=false).
notes: Follow-up work tracked in ENG-4680: add schema caching and pre-compilation for high-throughput endpoints; ENG-4691: improve error suggestion heuristics and localization. Hotfix followup: incident postmortem referenced for streaming regression during initial rollout (INC-2024-11-09) was addressed in runtime/streaming/handler.go.
